title: Greedy

views.title: Greedy
views.intro: Greedy is right when an exchange argument or a "stays ahead" invariant holds. State the argument in one sentence before coding; if you cannot, think DP. Typical shapes: furthest reach, sort by a key, two passes, ratio ordering, heap of options.
table: Candy, gas station style prefix logic

files.desc: Jump game I/II, gas station, candy, partition labels, queue reconstruction, cookies, largest number, units, valid parenthesis string, boats, refueling, straights, lemonade

pitfalls: Without a proof sketch, test the greedy against brute force on small inputs.
Largest Number: compare a+b with b+a, and special-case an all-zero result.
Valid Parenthesis String: carry a range [lo, hi] of possible open counts, not a single count.

decisions.q: Can you reach the end / minimum jumps?
Need the best past option when stuck?

calibration: SDE2 bar: jump game I/II, gas station, assign cookies, best time to buy and sell II, merge intervals.
SDE3 bar: candy, queue reconstruction, partition labels, largest number, task scheduler, valid parenthesis string, with a stated exchange argument.
Staff bar (for context): proving optimality or finding a counterexample fast, matroid-style greedy, and recognizing when greedy gives a good approximation but not an exact answer.
